notes: DIN 436 round-hole square washer. Rows with two disagreeing sources: M16 h (5; schrauben-lexikon 4), M22 h (6; schrauben-lexikon 5), M36 a and h (110/8; schrauben-lexikon 100/6) rest on fasteners.eu + globalfastener + boltport (boltport has a different size labelling, matched via d1) - treat those three cells as the weakest. fasteners.eu typo d1 '3' at M30 and d1 max 27,2 at M52 ignored. Square-hole version is DIN 436 V / DIN 440 V (not included). ASTM F844 not covered here.

verification.checks_done: Live re-fetch of fasteners.eu, torqbolt, globalfastener, schrauben-lexikon, boltport (+ fasten.it and digipich discovered via sibling records). Matrix 15 rows (M10..M52) x (d1,a,h) x 4 clusters (FE-cluster, GF, SL, FIT) = 45 cells. 41 cells have 4 clusters. The 4 weak cells the producer flagged (M16 h=5, M22 h=6, M36 a=110, M36 h=8) have exactly 3 clusters (FE, GF, FIT) against the sl dissent (4, 5, 100, 6); the producer's 3rd/4th source for them was boltport, which under the STRICT reading is the same cluster as fasteners.eu, so WITHOUT fasten.it these four cells would have only 2 clusters. M30 d1=33: GF, SL, FIT agree (fasteners.eu/torqbolt print '3' typo) -> 3 even excluding the fe cluster. Evidence sl is wrong at M36: its M36 column (a 100, h 6) duplicates M33's (100, 6) while all other sources have 110/8, and sl is the only one with a=100 twice; sl M16 h=4 / M22 h=5 break the otherwise monotone h series (3,4,5,5,6,6,...). Headers read: fe 'd1 nominal min / a nominal max / h nominal', fasten.it 'd nom=min / a max=nom / h nom', gf 'd min=nominal / s max=nominal (= side a) / h nominal', sl 'd / a / h'. Physical sanity: a > d1, d1,a,h monotone.
problems: CONDITIONAL: the record's own source list (fe+tq copy, gf, sl, boltport) gives only 2 clusters for M16 h, M22 h, M36 a, M36 h under the strict reading (boltport = fasteners.eu cluster) and sl contradicts them. They pass ONLY because fasten.it (verified live, all 15 rows equal the record) is a third independent cluster.
